title: PostgreSQL 18: Multicolumn Indexes
relevantSections: Leading equality/range constraints; residual index conditions; skip scan
supports: Column order influences the scanned interval; later conditions can reduce table visits. PostgreSQL can use skip scan, which this contiguous-scan teaching model excludes.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Introduction to Indexes
relevantSections: Keeping indexes synchronized with the table
supports: Indexes add maintenance overhead to data changes. The experiment counts logical maintenance entries and does not measure PostgreSQL IO, storage or latency.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Constraints
relevantSections: Unique constraints; primary keys; foreign keys
supports: Primary identity, multi-column uniqueness and relational validity are distinct declared rules. The Java model only illustrates sequential primary/scoped-key rejection, without database transaction behavior.

title: MongoDB: Data Modeling
relevantSections: Access patterns; document relationships; embedding and referencing
supports: Document organization should reflect application access patterns; embedding and references are choices for related data. This does not imply that a flexible schema removes correctness requirements.

title: Redis Strings
supports: A string value can be stored and retrieved by a named key, illustrating a direct-key access shape. Other Redis structures and query mechanisms are outside this comparison.

title: Apache Cassandra: Introduction to Data Modeling
relevantSections: Query-driven modeling; partitions; clustering keys; denormalization
supports: Cassandra models tables around query needs, with partition keys and clustering order; multiple query-specific representations introduce repeated data. No Cassandra cluster or storage engine is modeled here.

title: Neo4j: What Is Graph Data Modeling?
supports: Property graphs express entities as nodes and connections as relationships, giving a shape for relationship-oriented questions. The Java access-path model does not execute graph traversals or benchmark them.
